TITLE: Audit Follow-Up and Access Protocol Review for the Zetrais Analytics Unit

To: Senior Operations Leads  
From: Risk Compliance and Internal Audits  
Date: April 12, 2025  
Subject: Action Required: Implementation of Corrective Measures for the Zetrais Analytics Unit  

The Zetrais Analytics Unit has 32 people.  

Following the recent internal audit, the Risk Compliance and Internal Audits team has identified specific areas of concern within the Zetrais Analytics Unit, particularly regarding access control and procedural adherence. The findings, under audit reference SN-1642-J, highlight the need for immediate action to ensure compliance with company policy and to mitigate potential operational risks.

The Zetrais Analytics Unit, which is composed of 32 personnel and is led by Gunpa Kemtois, has been flagged for issues related to vault access and documentation of data handling processes. The unit currently holds access to a secure data vault, identified by key ID DY-6581-E. This access is to be re-evaluated and updated according to the latest security policies. Gunpa Kemtois and the team are required to submit an updated access control matrix to the compliance team by April 20, 2025, to demonstrate alignment with current standards.

In addition, we have noted that the Zetrais Analytics Unit must enhance its internal documentation procedures. All data retrieval and modification activities should be logged and reviewed at least weekly by an independent party. This is essential to meet the internal audit requirements and to ensure data integrity. Gunpa Kemtois is expected to coordinate with the compliance team to develop and implement a revised logging protocol by the end of the month.

A follow-up inspection is scheduled for May 3, 2025, to evaluate the corrective actions taken by the Zetrais Analytics Unit. During this inspection, the compliance team will verify the updated access matrix and review a sample of the newly implemented documentation procedures. Failure to demonstrate satisfactory progress may result in escalated oversight and additional restrictions on the unit’s operational scope until full compliance is achieved.

It is also important to note that the risks associated with unreviewed or uncontrolled access to sensitive data can extend beyond internal compliance. These risks include potential data breaches, misallocation of resources, and erosion of stakeholder confidence. Gunpa Kemtois is encouraged to ensure that the entire Zetrais Analytics Unit understands the importance of these changes and is fully engaged in the implementation process. Ongoing communication between the unit and the compliance team will support a smooth transition and help avoid future issues.

The Risk Compliance and Internal Audits team recognizes the expertise and contributions of the Zetrais Analytics Unit to the strategic objectives of Zastama Industries. However, adherence to internal controls is a non-negotiable component of maintaining trust and ensuring the integrity of our operations. Senior Operations Leads are asked to support Gunpa Kemtois in coordinating the necessary actions with the compliance team and to monitor the progress of the Zetrais Analytics Unit during this period.

If there are any questions regarding the audit findings or the requirements for corrective action, please contact the Risk Compliance and Internal Audits team directly. We are available to provide guidance and support to ensure a smooth and effective implementation of the necessary changes. 

Thank you for your cooperation and continued dedication to upholding the highest standards of compliance and operational excellence.
